data.narrative:
Cambridge Aerospace, a Series B defense and security company founded by Steven Barrett and Chris Sylvan, has raised $300M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 8 private Defense & Security peers at the same stage, supplemented by 2 public comps (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). The private peer set spans $300M to $3.0B in valuation, with a median of $1.1B; named comparables include Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), and Harmattan AI ($1.4B).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $300M total capital raised as a proxy base valuation, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implying $570M. Peer-median analysis directly benchmarks Cambridge Aerospace against 8 same-sector, same-stage private companies, yielding a $1.1B implied valuation. These methods produce a low of $484M (average of low-end estimates), a median of $848M, and a high of $1.3B (average of high-end estimates).

The $484M–$1.3B range reflects material dispersion within the peer set and inherent uncertainty in stage-progression timing. Cambridge Aerospace's valuation most likely clusters toward $848M, though position within the range depends on unobserved factors including revenue traction, technical differentiation within Defense & Security, and capital deployment efficiency relative to named peers.
